newsitem.title: DUBAI: WTO says UAE agrees to 15 pct import duty ceiling.
newsitem.headline: WTO says UAE agrees to 15 pct import duty ceiling.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates has agreed to an import duty ceiling of 15 percent on industrial and agricultural products, the deputy director-general of the World Trade Organisation said in an interview published on Monday.

"This commitment does not present any problem to the Emirates and in fact gives it sufficient flexibility for the future since the present actual import duties are either four percent or zero percent," Anwarul Hoda said, as quoted by the UAE daily Gulf News.

"If and when necessary the UAE can increase duties on different items up to 15 percent," he was quoted as saying on the sidelines of a conference in the capital Abu Dhabi on "The Implications of UAE Membership in the WTO".
The UAE has been a member of the WTO for less than a year.
Hoda said the UAE had committed itself to keeping duties on chemicals and pharmaceuticals between zero to 6.5 percent, but said these levels would only be applicable in 10 to 15 years.
"The UAE has not made any commitments to telecommunication services and its commitments to financial services are limited to the current situation," he was quoted as saying.
UAE officials have said that telecommunications, a strategic sector, would remain closed to outside investors.
Hoda said the UAE had no commitments to grant new licenses for operating bank branches in the oil-rich Gulf state or to expand activities of existing financial institutions.
There are 27 foreign banks, 15 representative offices and 19 local banks operating in the UAE.
